description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 60% to 80% and is linearly scaled. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 61% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rising to about 66% at 1000. The "MEND" method is shown as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at around 66% and increasing to approximately 74% by the end of the range. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 63% and rises to roughly 68%. The "MEMIT" method, indicated by a purple line with star markers, begins at approximately 66% and ends at around 72%. The "IKE" method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at about 65% and increases to roughly 70%. All lines show a general upward trend, with the "MEND" and "IKE" methods exhibiting the steepest increases early on, while "Base" shows the slowest growth. The "MEND" and "IKE" lines remain relatively flat at the higher end of the x-axis, while "MEMIT" continues to rise slightly.
